purpose_statement: This model exists to give the entire program engineering and management team - not just Ron - clear guidance on Design Input and Design Output CDRLs through every System Development Lifecycle phase and SETR maturity expectation. The core value isn't the list of DIDs; it's making visible how these documents work together back and forth, in sequence, across the whole team: early analysis (LORA, CMRS, FMECA, RM_PREDICTIONS) shapes design decisions, design maturity in turn reshapes that analysis, and the ECP process is what keeps everything synchronized after baseline. Every relationship field in this model (influences/influenced_by, maturity_states, confirmed_patterns) exists to make that back-and-forth explicit and visible in the eventual webapp - not to just catalog documents in isolation. Any future contributor to this model (human or AI) should treat capturing those cross-document dependencies as the primary goal, with the DID/event/level bookkeeping as the supporting structure that makes it renderable. Scope boundary (confirmed): the subway map graph (nodes + influences/influenced_by edges) covers PROCESS and PRODUCT ARTIFACTS only. Change-request objects (ECP, RFV, NOR, SCN, ERR) are explicitly out of that graph - they appear only as a lightweight cross-cutting badge/indicator on artifacts that require one before a given SETR event, never as their own station or edge-bearing node.
$schema_notes: Data model for SEMP 'subway map' figure showing CDRL/DID relationships across the SE Technical Review (SETR) sequence and CM baselines. Two primary lines: DESIGN_INPUT and DESIGN_OUTPUT. Support lines: MGMT, TEST, LOGISTICS, SAFETY_RELIABILITY, CM. Nodes = individual DIDs. Edges = directional influence relationships. 'station' = the SETR event/baseline where a DID is drafted, updated, or formally baselined.

setr_events.name: Software Specification Review
setr_events.notes: NAVAIR software-intensive SETR supplement (NAVAIRINST 4355.19 series) - reviews completeness of the software specification; this is where SRS gets baselined, ahead of PDR baselining the hardware/system Allocated Baseline. Not called out by name in NAVSEA's generic SETR handbook - confirm whether your program's SEP invokes the NAVAIR software supplement before treating this as a mandatory station.

SSR (Software Specification Review) was missing entirely from the initial SETR event list - not deliberately excluded, just not checked for. Confirmed via NAVAIRINST 4355.19 series as a real software-intensive SETR supplement sitting between SFR and PDR. Added as an event; moved SRS's baseline point from PDR to SSR accordingly. Note this event is NAVAIR-specific and not named in NAVSEA's generic SETR handbook - confirm applicability against your program's SEP.

maturity_state_legend.description: Every CDRL node carries a maturity_states array capturing the DRAFT/FINAL cadence (and, where the DID requires periodic resubmission, an UPDATE state) required by DoD 5010.12-M / the DID's own submission requirements. This is the actual per-station marker data the chart renders - distinct from the separate live per-program status overlay (draft/submitted/approved) discussed for the 'CDRL Path' tracking feature.

states.DRAFT: Preliminary version submitted for government review ahead of a SETR event - not yet approved as a controlled baseline artifact.
states.FINAL: Approved/baselined version - establishes or updates a CM baseline (Functional/Allocated/Product) or otherwise becomes the controlled version of record at that event.
states.UPDATE: A required resubmission after FINAL, tied to a later SETR event or milestone rather than a one-time deliverable. Some CDRLs (SEMP, IMP/IMS, RVTM, SAR/SSHAR) update at every subsequent review rather than going final once.
states.AS_NEEDED: Event-driven rather than review-driven (e.g., ECP) - doesn't follow the standard DRAFT/FINAL/UPDATE cadence tied to SETR events.

recommended_chart_rendering.DRAFT: hollow/outline station marker on the line
recommended_chart_rendering.FINAL: filled station marker on the line, larger if it also establishes a CM baseline
recommended_chart_rendering.UPDATE: filled marker with a ring/halo, repeating at each recurrence point
recommended_chart_rendering.AS_NEEDED: diamond marker floating off the main line rather than an inline station, since it isn't tied to a fixed SETR position

maturity_state_legend.note: Where at_event is a range or 'recurring': true, the chart should render one marker per matching SETR event rather than a single fixed station - e.g., RVTM's UPDATE state should appear at SFR, SSR, PDR, CDR, and TRR, not just once.

confirmation_status.method: Walked event-by-event (SRR through PCA) confirming each CDRL, DID number, and title against the model.
confirmation_status.result: All 9 populated SETR events (SRR, SFR, SSR, PDR, CDR, TRR, SVR_FCA, PRR, PCA) confirmed as-is, no changes.
confirmation_status.ASR_ISR_note: ASR and ISR intentionally carry no CDRLs in this model - confirmed as correct, not a gap.

decomposition_dimension.description: Third dimension orthogonal to SETR-event (time) and Design Input/Output (line): where in the system decomposition a given CDRL instance applies. Most system-level artifacts (SSS, SEMP, etc.) exist once. CI-level and below recur once PER applicable CI - the chart should treat these as a 'drill-down' from the System-level default view, not permanent extra lines.

levels.notes: Optional intermediate level - no Segment level used on this program.
This is where MIL-STD-961E spec-type maturity (Type B -> Type C) actually lives. One instance per CI.
Typically documented inside the parent CI's design description (SDD, drawings) rather than as its own separate CDRL.
Lowest level; almost never a standalone CDRL - internal structure of the SDD/DBDD.

decomposition_dimension.recommended_chart_interaction: Level filter/toggle on the existing zoomable map, not a separate stacked map. Default view = SYSTEM level. Selecting a specific CI 'drills down' to reveal that CI's own Dev-Spec -> Product-Spec progression, consistent with the GPS zoom metaphor already chosen for SETR-event granularity.
decomposition_dimension.gap_identified: The event-by-event confirmation walkthrough only validated nodes already in the model - it did not surface CI-level artifacts because the model had no decomposition axis at all. The two most significant missing nodes (per MIL-STD-961E) are added below: the CI-level Development Specification (Type B) and Product Specification (Type C), which is the actual 'developmental spec -> production spec' progression Ron described.

removed_nodes.reason: Removed per Ron - not applicable to this program.

confirmed_patterns.ECP_driven_update_pattern: For baselined requirements/design docs, UPDATE maturity is typically NOT a fixed single re-baseline event - it's handled via the ECP process and reviewed at minimum at every subsequent SETR event through PRR. Applied so far to: SSS, IRS. Check this pattern against each subsequent baselined document rather than assuming a single UPDATE event.
confirmed_patterns.MGMT_no_draft_pattern: SEMP, IMP/IMS, and RMP have no separate DRAFT maturity state - they are delivered as FINAL starting at SRR, then updated at every subsequent SETR event. SEP is the exception, tied to Milestones rather than SETR events.
confirmed_patterns.no_as_built_state_pattern: Reverted an earlier addition - there is no separate AS_BUILT maturity state. PCA is simply the final SETR event in a document's normal UPDATE cadence (via ECP), same as any other post-baseline revision. Applies to ENG_DRAWINGS and HW_PROD_SPEC; check this against any other CI-level design-output artifact still carrying an AS_BUILT reference.
confirmed_patterns.analysis_derived_docs_pattern: LORA and CMRS (and likely other ILS/specialty-engineering analysis products) don't follow the ECP-through-PRR update cadence used by core design docs. Instead: (1) no independent update schedule, (2) if they change, it's in lockstep with an ECP against a related design input or design output document, and (3) the relationship is bidirectional - draft-stage analysis feeds design decisions (design-for-X), while final analysis content is in turn shaped by the as-designed system. Check this pattern against other analysis-type CDRLs (FMECA, RM_PREDICTIONS, SSHAR) as they come up for review, since they may follow the same logic rather than the ECP-recurring-update pattern currently assigned to them.
confirmed_patterns.relationship_assessment_status: influences/influenced_by fields were populated in a single pass by Claude based on standard SE domain reasoning, not confirmed individually with Ron like the DID/event mappings were. These should be reviewed together, especially the ECP node (currently modeled as influencing/being influenced by nearly everything, which may be too broad to be useful in the actual chart) and any node where the relationship crosses from LOGISTICS/SAFETY_RELIABILITY back into DESIGN_INPUT/DESIGN_OUTPUT lines, since those cross-line edges are exactly the 'back and forth' Ron identified as the core value of this model.
confirmed_patterns.station_summary_generation: station_summary_by_setr_event is now PROGRAMMATICALLY DERIVED from each node's maturity_states array, not hand-maintained. Regenerate it any time a node's maturity_states change, rather than editing both places - this eliminates the drift found during the 2026-08-08 verification pass (15 issues, mostly stale summary entries).
confirmed_patterns.multi_level_maturity_pattern: Some documents (confirmed so far: RVTM) mature at different SETR events depending on decomposition level - System-level and CI-level instances of the same document type follow different DRAFT->FINAL timing. These use 'maturity_states_by_level' (a dict keyed by decomposition level) instead of the flat 'maturity_states' array. The station_summary generator now handles both formats, rendering multi-level nodes with a level tag e.g. 'RVTM[SYS](draft)' vs 'RVTM[CI](final)'.

Clicking should reveal the full record from the top-level 'superseded_dids' array (canceled DID number, title, canceling authority, and source).

This is a first-class feature, not an afterthought - Ron's authoritative schedule is expected to supersede much of the manually-interviewed content in this model.

change_request_mechanisms.scope_note: ECP, RFV, and NOR (plus SCN and ERR, included for completeness) are change-request OBJECTS, not process or product engineering artifacts. Per Ron's explicit scope decision, they are excluded from the subway map's node/edge graph entirely. Their only role in the visualization is as a cross-cutting GROUPING INDICATOR - i.e., flagging which process/product artifacts require one of these change-request objects to be updated ahead of a given SETR event - not as first-class stations with their own influence relationships.

Clicking the badge could show which mechanism applies and at which SETR events, without cluttering the main influence graph.

temporal_marker_types.description: Not every CDRL due date is tied to a SETR event. Three distinct temporal marker types exist in this model:

types.SETR_EVENT: Tied to a specific technical review (ASR, SRR, SFR, etc.) - the majority of engineering artifacts.
types.MILESTONE: Tied to an acquisition Milestone (A/B/C) rather than a SETR event - e.g., SEP, TEMP.
types.CONTRACT_DAY: Tied to a fixed number of days/months after contract award (e.g., 3 MAC = 3 Months After Contract), independent of any review or milestone. Often the EARLIEST due dates in the whole program, predating ASR.
types.MANAGEMENT_TRACK: Recurring on a periodic cadence (e.g., annual, per subsequent Milestone) rather than tied to a single fixed point.

temporal_marker_types.chart_implication: CONTRACT_DAY markers should render as their own leftmost station(s) on the map, before ASR, not folded into the SETR event sequence.

external_review_boards.description: Safety-domain artifacts are additionally paced by external review boards, not just SETR events. These occur loosely BEFORE the SETR event they're associated with, not at the same time.

boards.name: Weapon System Explosives Safety Review Board

external_review_boards.chart_implication: Safety-line UPDATE markers tied to these boards should note the board+phase explicitly (e.g., 'WSESRB/SSSTRP Design Review, ~pre-CDR') rather than being flattened to the SETR event itself, since the actual review happens beforehand.

import_schema.description: Defines how an external, authoritative CDRL schedule (Ron's own JSON export, including RACI) gets imported/merged into this model - either by a future Code Chat feature or manually in a follow-up session.
import_schema.external_key_field: Key - acronym/initials matching (or closely matching) this model's node 'id' field.
matching_strategy: 2. Alias match: check node.aliases array for a match if exact match fails.

3. Unmatched: if neither matches, do NOT silently create a new node or drop the record - flag it in an 'unmatched_import_records' list for manual reconciliation. New CDRLs discovered this way should go through the same DID-verification rigor as everything else in this model, not be auto-added.

field_merge_behavior.raci: TRUSTED OVERRIDE - Ron's schedule is authoritative for RACI, import directly.
field_merge_behavior.maturity_states / at_event timing: TRUSTED OVERRIDE - Ron's schedule is authoritative for SETR-event timing, import directly, but log a diff against whatever was previously in the model (many nodes here are still first-pass/interview-confirmed and may conflict).
field_merge_behavior.did / title: FLAG CONFLICTS - if the import's DID or title differs from what's already confirmed in this model, do NOT silently overwrite; surface both values for Ron to reconcile, since this model's DID numbers were individually verified against DLA ASSIST/EverySpec.
field_merge_behavior.influences / influenced_by / decompositi: PRESERVE - these are Claude-assessed and likely not present in Ron's schedule at all; the import should add RACI/timing on top of the existing model, not replace these fields.

raci_schema.responsible: string - single role/org who does the work
raci_schema.accountable: string - single role/org with sign-off authority
raci_schema.consulted: array of strings - roles/orgs consulted during development
raci_schema.informed: array of strings - roles/orgs kept informed of status

import_schema.audit_trail_requirement: Every import run should produce a log entry (timestamp, source filename, count of matched/unmatched/conflicting records) rather than silently merging - this model has already been hand-corrected many times today and needs a clear 'what changed and why' record, not a silent overwrite.

update_pathways.description: Two supported ways to update this model: BATCH_IMPORT (Ron's authoritative CDRL schedule JSON, many records at once) and ATOMIC_EDIT (single field/node change made directly in the webapp UI). Both must converge on the same validation and audit mechanism so the model can't drift between the two paths.
shared_requirements: Both pathways run the SAME validation function before committing - the consistency checks already proven out today (no dangling influences/influenced_by references, valid SETR event IDs, no duplicate DIDs, every node has maturity_states or is explicitly exempt). Do not implement two separate validation code paths that could drift apart.
Both pathways write an audit log entry: timestamp, source (batch-import filename OR 'atomic-edit'), which node(s)/field(s) changed, before/after values.
Both pathways update the SAME underlying JSON - there is only one reference model, not a separate copy per pathway.

BATCH_IMPORT.trigger: User uploads/pastes Ron's CDRL schedule JSON.
BATCH_IMPORT.behavior: See 'import_schema' section - matches by Key, applies trusted-override/flag-conflict/preserve rules per field, processes many nodes in one pass.
BATCH_IMPORT.persistence: Same open question as ATOMIC_EDIT below - see 'persistence_mechanism_decision_needed'.

ATOMIC_EDIT.trigger: User clicks a station in the webapp (Zoom Level 3 detail panel) and edits a single field - e.g., correcting a DRAFT event, adding a RACI entry, adding a note.
ATOMIC_EDIT.behavior: Single-node, single-field change, applied and validated immediately, with an inline undo option since there's no natural 'previous file version' to fall back to like batch import has.
ATOMIC_EDIT.persistence: Same open question as BATCH_IMPORT above - see 'persistence_mechanism_decision_needed'.

persistence_mechanism_decision_needed.problem: A browser-based React app cannot write directly to a file in your GitHub repo. This wasn't resolved when we originally decided on file-based JSON persistence, and it applies equally to atomic edits and batch imports.

options.option: Export/Download updated JSON, Ron manually commits
options.tradeoff: Simplest to build, zero new infrastructure, but re-introduces a manual step and re-opens the door to the exact drift/sync problem we just fixed with the auto-regenerated station summary.

options.option: Local dev-only file-write via a small Node/Express backend running alongside the React app
options.tradeoff: Real file persistence during local development, but adds a backend component to what was scoped as a standalone React app, and doesn't help once deployed anywhere off your dev machine.

options.option: GitHub API integration - webapp commits directly to the repo on save
options.tradeoff: Cleanest long-term solution and keeps the repo as the single source of truth, but requires a GitHub token/auth flow and real write-access handling - meaningfully more scope than originally discussed.

persistence_mechanism_decision_needed.recommendation: Start with Export/Download for v1 (fastest to working software), explicitly flagged as a known limitation, with GitHub API integration as a fast-follow if atomic edits turn out to be frequent enough that manual re-commit becomes a real friction point.
persistence_mechanism_decision_needed.status: DECIDED - Export/Download for v1, confirmed by Ron 2026-08-08. GitHub API integration deferred as a fast-follow if atomic-edit frequency justifies it.
